title: Diagnostics Hardware Report
description: Seven-part homelab inspection: dated physical drive evidence plus live Talos, Kubernetes, VPA, Longhorn, Argo and backup telemetry. Physical monitoring gaps remain explicit.

options.content:
**Live graphs are Talos guest telemetry. Physical drive evidence is dated.** Prometheus has no Proxmox SMART, physical-disk or NAS/ZFS feed; a green guest graph is not a physical-drive health check. Select a node or namespace above to narrow the supported live panels. Physical inventory and repair notes retain their own dates and are not filtered.

Work through the seven numbered sections. Click any drive below for its complete evidence, replacement constraints and verification steps. **No telemetry means unknown**, including a stopped node or crashing pod—not zero utilization or good health.

options.content:
**Inventory timestamp: Sep 9 22:00 UTC.** 75 of 76 inventoried PVCs with Longhorn replica configuration request one replica. The original September 8 inspection found 78/80 volumes configured with one copy; retained volumes and temporary backup clones explain why PVC and volume totals differ.

There is **no exported Longhorn desired-replica-count metric** here. Healthy means the configured target is met, not that a second copy exists. The original Coroot Keeper audit found its three processes on one physical host. Recheck actual placement before any drain or replica changes.

HP SFF / sda · PNY CS900 1TB SSD

options.content: ← Return to all seven diagnostic sections ## HP SFF · /dev/sda **PNY CS900 1TB SSD · 1,000 GB** **P1 · Investigate control-plane latency** Latest hardware observation: **Sep 9 22:01 UTC**. Fresh physical inspection; live SMART is not exported. ### Why this drive matters The etcd commit path was slow; the SSD is one candidate, not a proven sole cause. **Role:** Control-plane storage **Physical → guest → workload path:** PNY → hp-sff-cp → VM101 scsi0 100GiB → Talos .79 sda6 → etcd Mapping checked: Sep 8 23:53 UTC. ### Evidence and current versus baseline - Baseline etcd p99 was 43.8 ms (worst sampled 59.9 ms over 24 hours); host CPU contention is a separate candidate. - September 9 at 22:00 UTC: etcd fsync p99 42.26 ms and backend commit p99 60.52 ms; source attribution still requires physical/CPU correlation. - Fresh hardware check 2026-09-09T22:01:42.472617+00:00: SMART overall passed; temperature 33°C; power-on hours 24,616 h. - Fresh 55-second passive I/O: reads 0.027 MiB/s, writes 0.761 MiB/s, queue 0.257; workload-dependent, not a saturation benchmark. | Physical health field | Sep8 baseline | Latest observation | |---|---|---| | SMART overall | Passed | Passed | | Temperature °C | 33 | 33 | | Power-on hours | 24,594 | 24,616 | | Passive block-I/O average | Sep8 baseline | Latest sample | |---|---:|---:| | Read await, ms | 11.583 | 3.583 | | Write await, ms | 3.782 | 2.025 | | Busy, % | 15.649 | 10.783 | | Average queue | 0.378 | 0.257 | Latest passive sample: Sep 9 22:01 UTC–Sep 9 22:02 UTC, 55.001 seconds. Workload-dependent averages are **not fsync p99** or a saturation benchmark. An old load spike alone does not establish a failed SSD. ### Impact and urgency Slow or unavailable etcd can delay API writes and reconciliation across the cluster. ### Options - Compare etcd fsync with physical latency and Proxmox CPU steal under the same workload. - If storage remains the bottleneck, move the control-plane disk to compatible storage with documented power-loss protection. ### Capacity, fit and migration constraints - The control-plane guest disk is 100 GiB; verify source volume layout and recovery before migration. - Do not split the working enterprise mirror merely to obtain a drive. ### What proves the repair or replacement worked - Recheck the same persistent drive identity, health counters and relevant workload under comparable load. - Before a move or replacement, confirm recoverable backups and independent surviving replicas. **Confidence:** Hardware identity and baseline observations verified; replacement decisions distinguish measured symptoms from preventive changes.
